beyondthehorizon.options.title: Beyond the Terrain Settings
beyondthehorizon.options.enabled.tooltip: Heightmap LOD: draws the terrain beyond the render distance as a smooth heightmap (with the Block Heightmap and the trees on its finest tiles). Needs the mod on the server too (singleplayer: the client is enough).
beyondthehorizon.options.distance.toolti: How far the Heightmap LOD is drawn, in chunks (24 - 10000). Type a number. The fog ends at this distance.
beyondthehorizon.options.sharpness.toolt: How far out finer tiles are used. Higher is sharper and slower.
beyondthehorizon.options.start_level.too: Blocks per cell of the finest tiles. Larger is faster, smaller is sharper near the render distance.
beyondthehorizon.options.max_tiles.toolt: Most pieces (tiles) of the Heightmap LOD kept in graphics memory at once. Lower it if memory runs out, raise it if far terrain reloads as you move.
beyondthehorizon.options.fog_mode.toolti: Whose fog the terrain has at the end of the view.
beyondthehorizon.options.fog_start.toolt: Where the fog starts, in percent of where it ends.
beyondthehorizon.options.water_fog.toolt: Whether the terrain has the fog of water when seen from under it.
beyondthehorizon.options.tree_density.to: How many trees there are, in percent of the default. Changes apply at once: the loaded tiles are rebuilt.
beyondthehorizon.options.block_heightmap: Block Heightmap on or off: the finest tiles near you are drawn as columns of the heightmap (flat tops, walls between them), like blocks, instead of the smooth ground. How far it reaches is the distance below. Changes apply at once: the loaded tiles are rebuilt.

How far from you the terrain is Block Heightmap columns, in chunks. The tiles out to here are kept fine (2 blocks), whatever the sharpness: a big distance means many more tiles to load and draw (see Max tiles). Changes apply at once.
beyondthehorizon.options.trees.tooltip: Approximated trees on or off (not the real trees): boxes and sprites close to you up to the tree distance, flat billboard sprites beyond it. Changes apply at once: the loaded tiles are rebuilt.
beyondthehorizon.options.tree_distance.t: How far from you the trees are 3D (boxes), in chunks; the tiles out to here are kept fine enough for them, whatever the sharpness. Beyond it the trees are flat billboard sprites. Changes apply at once.
beyondthehorizon.options.pixel_filter.to: Pixelates the ground colors: the smooth blend is read on a grid 2, 4 or 8 times finer than the terrain samples, with a little noise for a textured look.
beyondthehorizon.options.server_settings: The settings of the tile server of this world (beyond-the-terrain-server.json).
Only available in a singleplayer world. A dedicated server is set up in its beyond-the-terrain-server.json.
beyondthehorizon.server.title: Beyond the Terrain Server Settings
beyondthehorizon.server.rejoin: Beyond the Terrain: server settings saved. Threads, priority and caches apply when you rejoin the world.
beyondthehorizon.server.generator_thread: Threads that generate the Heightmap LOD. Auto uses all cores but one, at least two. Applies when you rejoin the world.
beyondthehorizon.server.generator_priori: Java priority of the generator threads, 1 (lowest) to 9. Higher gets more CPU time against the game, chunk generation and other mods. They still pause for late frames. Applies when you rejoin the world.
beyondthehorizon.server.in_flight_per_th: Tiles handed to the generator for each thread before it reports back. More keeps the threads busy when the server thread is late, fewer reacts faster when you move. Applies at once.
beyondthehorizon.server.max_in_flight.to: The least number of tiles a player may have in flight. The setting per thread raises it when it gives more. Applies at once.
beyondthehorizon.server.max_queued.toolt: How many tile requests of one player wait on the server. Applies at once.
beyondthehorizon.server.min_level.toolti: The finest tile level the server generates. Higher levels are coarser and faster. Players learn it when they rejoin the world.
beyondthehorizon.server.max_distance.too: How far from a player the server generates the Heightmap LOD, in steps of 1 000 blocks. Applies at once.
beyondthehorizon.server.enabled.tooltip: Turns the Heightmap LOD of this server on or off. Players learn it when they rejoin the world.
beyondthehorizon.server.builds.tooltip: Where the real world is known (explored chunks), villages, other structures and what players built are drawn as part of the Heightmap LOD, as Block Heightmap columns that guess their look from the heights and the block colors. Off, they are left out and the generated terrain shows. Applies at once; players see it for tiles they load again, or after clearing the terrain cache.
beyondthehorizon.server.builds_level.too: The biggest tiles that still show builds, apart from the terrain quality: a tile is 32 blocks wide at the finest level, so builds are drawn near the explored world and fade out into plain terrain farther away. Higher shows them farther, at a cost in generation. Applies at once.
beyondthehorizon.server.pregen_threads.t: Generator threads while the Heightmap LOD is generated ahead by /farplane pregen distant. Auto uses all cores but one. Applies when the next generation starts.
beyondthehorizon.server.disk_cache.toolt: Keeps generated tiles in the world folder, so the next visit loads them instead of generating them. Applies when you rejoin the world.
beyondthehorizon.server.memory_cache.too: Tiles kept in the memory of the server. Applies when you rejoin the world.
